questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Make an application at
www.sio.no
, which handles all student housing. And make it in well advance, even before you know if you will be going on an exchange or not, since the housing is being offered via the "first come, first served" principle

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was living in Kringsjå, the biggest student housing area. Close to nature and still only 15 min away from centre by T-bane (metro)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

Take some kind of norwegian courses, or course about norwegian culture.
The lecturers in EU competition law were very competent.
Maritime law courses also good with different guest lecturers, but lacking an overall leadership from UiOs side

Take advantage of activities offered by SiO

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The language - it sounds so nice
The wollen sweaters :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for a student housing as soon as possible! My semester started in August, but I applied for housing in March already. However, housing offers wont be send out before end of June

During the intro week, you will be assigned to a buddy group. Make sure to participate in a lot of activities with your fellow buddies

Taking a language course at UiO is a good way to get to know other students from other faculties

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
My telephone SIM card from Denmark worked perfectly in Norway during the 5 months exchange, so no need to buy a new one
Use the app "Ruter" for public transportation in Oslo

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The language course I took on an voluntary basis, becuase of the people I met there

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Using the healthcare system can be a bit difficult when not having a national security number. But SiO offers a health service for students

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just go there, you won't regret :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
